title: Mutant Menace — Upgrade Options
summary: The Wise Mothman puts +1/+1 counters on creatures whenever nonland cards are milled from any library, and its rad counters make every player mill each turn. A shared removal package fixes the stock list's thin interaction; each direction then spends 6 more swaps on one plan. Budget: up to €30 per deck in total (Cardmarket prices).

notes: Curve shape is fine for a 4-mana commander, but several 2-drops (Power Fist, Nuka-Nuke Launcher, Biomass Mutation) don't affect the board.
Lumbering Megasloth (MV 12) and Agent Frank Horrigan (MV 7) are the clunkiest cards at the top.
Mana is fine: 39 lands + ~8 ramp. Many lands enter tapped (Temples, Opulent Palace, Tainted lands); improving them is a separate project.
Biggest weakness: only 5 spot removal and just 2 instant-speed answers.

Engine ledger — enablers: Ruin Crab, Mindcrank and the rad counters Mothman hands out all mill; payoffs: Mothman turns each nonland mill into +1/+1 counters, Kami of Whispered Hopes adds one to each, Evolution Sage proliferates on landfall and Evolution Witness buys permanents back. Support: the four removal instants. The mill half is genuinely self-feeding — rad's life loss feeds Mindcrank, which mills again.

The throttled half: Ruin Crab and Evolution Sage are landfall triggers and the deck plays exactly zero extra land drops, so each fires once a turn. Two extra-drop enablers (Loot, Exuberant Explorer €1.47 and Oracle of Mul Daya €2.58) would roughly double both cards for about €4 — the only purchase worth making in this deck.

Win conditions (finishers in the 99, counted by the deck-comparison skill's rule): big threats — Alpha Deathclaw, Screeching Scorchbeast, Strong, the Brutish Thespian, Agent Frank Horrigan, Lumbering Megasloth, Lily Bowen, Raging Grandma, Bloatfly Swarm, Rampaging Yao Guai; team closers — Biomass Mutation, Vault 12: The Necropolis; mill — Fraying Sanity.

core.name: Core interaction package
core.description: Four cheap instants that go in whichever direction you choose. Spot removal goes from 5 to 9, with 6 at instant speed.

swaps.why: Instant: destroy any permanent an opponent controls, for 2 mana. Megasloth costs 12 minus the counters in play, which you can rarely make cheap.
Kill a creature with no counters on it, or remove up to three counters from one. Biomass is a combat trick that mostly duplicates what your counters already do.
Instant: destroy any permanent; its controller gets a 3/3. Bobblehead is a 3-mana rock whose counter ability is slow.
Flexible: destroy a monocoloured creature, an artifact or an enchantment, or draw 2 and discard 1. Theta fits the theme but needs crewing; this was the closest cut.

directions.name: Counter Engine
directions.pitch: Mothman puts +1/+1 counters on your creatures whenever nonland cards are milled, so make every player mill as often as you can: Ruin Crab on each of your lands, Mesmeric Orb on each untap, Mindcrank and The Master of Lake-town on each life loss, and rad counters in each player's own first main phase. The Water Crystal adds four cards to every opponent's mill, which makes decking the table a real win; Evolution Sage, Inexorable Tide and Tekuthal proliferate the counters, and Evolution Witness and Hollowmurk Siege keep the cards coming. It struggles when Mothman is removed again and again, and Mesmeric Orb mills you too, so watch your own library.
directions.plays_like: Big creatures attacking; draws lots of cards

swaps.why: Each land that enters under your control mills each opponent 3 (7 with The Water Crystal). Simultaneous mills trigger Mothman once, counting every nonland card milled, so that's counters on about 6 creatures per land drop. Acolyte's ward 1 is a small effect.
+1 extra counter on every placement, and it taps for mana equal to its power, so Mothman's counters turn it into a big mana source. Power Fist needs equip mana and a successful hit.
Whenever it gets +1/+1 counters (Mothman does that constantly), return a permanent card from your graveyard to your hand. Repeatable card advantage. The Launcher's equip 3 is too expensive.

Proliferates on every land drop: more +1/+1 counters on your creatures and more rad counters on opponents. Watchful Radstag only copies itself when a bigger creature enters; Mothman's counters don't count.

Whenever an opponent loses life, they mill that many cards. Rad-counter mills cost 1 life per nonland card milled, so rad mills and combat hits mill again, and each mill is another Mothman trigger; with Syr Konrad, damage and mill feed each other. Piper only does anything when she deals combat damage.
Land swap. Untapped green or blue on its own. Overflowing Basin can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Untapped black or green on its own. Viridescent Bog can't make mana by itself ({1},{T} only).
Land swap. Untapped blue or black. Temple of the False God only makes colourless mana, and only with five lands out.

how_to_play.summary: Win in the air with counter-loaded Mothman, Tekuthal and Screeching Scorchbeast, by decking the table with Mesmeric Orb and The Water Crystal, with Syr Konrad chaining off Mindcrank, or with twenty growth counters on Simic Ascendancy. The board you want is Mothman plus a repeatable mill source (Ruin Crab, Mesmeric Orb or rad counters), so every turn puts counters on your creatures.

sections.title: How Mothman and rad counters work
points: Mothman: when it enters or attacks, each player gets a rad counter. Whenever nonland cards are milled, put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to X target creatures (X = nonland cards milled). Several players milling at once (Ruin Crab, Raul) triggers it once, counting all of them; each separate mill, such as each Mesmeric Orb trigger, triggers it again.

Rad counters: a player with rad counters mills that many cards at the start of their own first main phase, so each player's counters fire once a round, on their turn, not every turn. For each nonland card milled they lose 1 life and remove one rad counter; milled lands don't remove counters. A few counters are usually gone within a turn or two (in one go with The Water Crystal, which adds four cards and more life loss), so keep adding more.

sections.title: Turns 1–3: mill sources and ramp
points: Ruin Crab: each land that enters under your control mills each opponent 3, including lands from Farseek, Rampant Growth, Cultivate, Evolving Wilds and Tato Farmer.
Mindcrank: whenever an opponent loses life, they mill that many, so combat damage and rad life loss mill again. The Master of Lake-town does the same for every player, you included.

Tato Farmer: its rad counters are optional, so usually decline them. Tap it to put a land card milled this turn from any graveyard onto the battlefield under your control: ramp plus an extra landfall for Ruin Crab and Evolution Sage. It untaps only on your turn, so that's once a round; use it on whichever turn a land gets milled.
Ramp: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talismans, Farseek, Rampant Growth, Cultivate.

sections.title: Turn 4: Mothman
points: From now on every mill that hits a nonland card triggers Mothman: Ruin Crab on your land drops, Mindcrank on life loss, and each player's own rad mill on their turn.

Spread counters, evasive creatures first: Mothman and Tekuthal (flying), Infesting Radroach, Nightkin Ambusher. Nightkin can't be blocked while the defending player has a rad counter; attack alongside Mothman, whose attack trigger gives them one before blockers are declared.

sections.title: Keeping rad counters going
points: Proliferate: Evolution Sage on every land, Inexorable Tide on every spell, Karn's Bastion for four mana; Tekuthal doubles each one, and Agent Frank Horrigan proliferates twice when it enters or attacks. Protect them.

Attack triggers: Mothman (each player +1) and Screeching Scorchbeast (each player +2). Hitting a player: Glowing One (+4), Infesting Radroach (+damage dealt), Vexing Radgull (+2, or proliferate if they already have some).

Bursts: Nightkin Ambusher (+4) and The Master and Mirelurk Queen (+2) to one target player; Vault 12 (each player +3), Nuclear Fallout (+X each), Feral Ghoul on death (each opponent, equal to its power), Bloatfly Swarm when damaged.
When you proliferate, add to opponents and skip yourself unless you want the mill.

sections.title: Engines and card draw
points: Boosters: Hardened Scales, Kami of Whispered Hopes, Winding Constrictor; doublers: Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution.

Hollowmurk Siege (choose Sultai): draw the first time each turn a counter goes on one of your creatures, and Mothman triggers on every player's turn. Mirelurk Queen also draws once a turn off any nonland mill.

Struggle for Project Purity (choose Brotherhood): about 3 cards each upkeep; the opponents' extra draw only speeds up the mill. Marcus, Guardian Project and Evolution Witness (a permanent card back from your graveyard each time it gets counters) add more.

Fraying Sanity: curse the opponent whose graveyard fills fastest. At every end step they mill as many cards as went to their graveyard that turn (four more with The Water Crystal), which is another Mothman trigger.

sections.title: Closing the game
points: Screeching Scorchbeast: once each turn, when nonland cards are milled, you may create that many 2/2 Zombies. Skip small mills and take a big one, such as a Ruin Crab trigger with The Water Crystal out.

Simic Ascendancy gets a growth counter for every +1/+1 counter put on your creatures, so one Mothman trigger across five creatures with Hardened Scales out is ten. Proliferate adds to it directly. You win at your upkeep with twenty or more; keep Counterspell or Mutational Advantage up to protect it.

Decking: Mesmeric Orb with The Water Crystal, Fraying Sanity and Ruin Crab empty libraries fast (see the bracket 3 notes). A player loses when they have to draw from an empty library, and Struggle for Project Purity makes each opponent draw at your upkeep.

sections.title: Your turn and tips
points: Your own rad mill happens at the start of your first main phase, after Mesmeric Orb's upkeep mills, so those counters arrive before combat. Play your land before combat (Ruin Crab, Evolution Sage), then attack with Mothman.

You get rad counters too, from Mothman, Screeching Scorchbeast, Vault 12, Nuclear Fallout and Bloatfly Swarm, and Winding Constrictor gives you one extra each time. Watch your library and life, especially with Mesmeric Orb and The Master of Lake-town, which mill you as well. Strong makes you gain life from radiation instead.
Nuclear Fallout gives each creature −2X/−2X; your counter-loaded creatures often survive.

Hold up instant-speed answers for the end of an opponent's turn or a key threat: Counterspell and Drown in the Loch (it counts the target controller's graveyard, which the mill fills), Assassin's Trophy, Beast Within, Putrefy, Atomize and Sultai Charm. Binding the Old Gods destroys a nonland permanent now and fetches a Forest next turn, another landfall.
Mulligan hands without 3+ lands and some ramp; you want Mothman on turn 4.

directions.name: Mill Them Out
directions.pitch: Empty opponents' libraries while their rad counters drain their life. Mothman's counters give you a combat plan as backup.
directions.plays_like: Quiet early, then decks the table

swaps.why: Each land you play mills every opponent 3.
A second land-mill Crab. Power Fist does nothing for a mill plan.

Every time an opponent mills, they mill 4 more, and its activated ability mills each opponent your hand size. A budget Bruvac ($3 instead of $41). Harold and Bob gives you rad counters, the wrong direction.
Each card you draw mills an opponent 2, and it repeats if the milled cards share a colour. Radstag is inconsistent.
Each card you draw mills every opponent 2. Strong irradiates you, the opposite of this plan.
{1}{B}: each player mills a card. Every creature card that hits a graveyard pings each opponent for 1. Mill and damage in one card. Frank is strong but costs 7.

how_to_play.summary: Empty opponents' libraries while their rad counters drain their life; Mothman's counters are the combat backup plan.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Ruin Crab and Hedron Crab: each land you play mills 3 (every opponent and one player respectively).
Draw-to-mill: Sphinx's Tutelage (each card you draw mills an opponent 2, repeating on shared colours) and Psychic Corrosion (each card you draw mills each opponent 2).
The Water Crystal: every opponent mill becomes mill +4. Syr Konrad: {1}{B} makes each player mill a card and pings opponents when creature cards hit graveyards.

sections.title: Tips
points: Prioritise card draw: every card you draw is a mill with the Tutelages.
Target the opponent with the smallest library first; one empty library means one player can't draw.
Keep enough blockers: this version wins slowly and doesn't race well.

directions.name: Graveyard Value
directions.pitch: Mill yourself on purpose, then replay what's in your graveyard. Your own mill still gives Mothman counters, and you can get back removal you've already used.
directions.plays_like: Grinds out long games; hard to stop

swaps.why: Mills you 3 when it enters and 3 more when it dies, for 1 mana.
Mills you 3, then can return a creature to your hand when it dies.
Returns any card from your graveyard to your hand, including spent removal.
Gives a card, a Treasure or a 2/2 Zombie whenever cards leave your graveyard.
Mills you 3 when it enters or attacks, and makes a 2/2 Zombie whenever creatures are milled.
Each turn, replay a land and one permanent of each type from your graveyard.

how_to_play.summary: Mill yourself on purpose, then replay creatures and permanents from the graveyard; your own mill still triggers Mothman.

sections.title: Game plan
points: Self-mill: Stitcher's Supplier (3 on enter and on death), Undead Butler (3, then returns a creature when it dies), Sidisi (3 on enter and attack, plus a Zombie when creatures are milled).
Recursion: Muldrotha replays a permanent of each type from your graveyard every turn; Eternal Witness returns any card (including spent removal).
Teval's Judgment gives a card, a Treasure or a Zombie whenever cards leave your graveyard.

sections.title: Tips
points: Mill yourself before casting Muldrotha or Eternal Witness so the best targets are there.
Watch for opponents' graveyard hate (e.g. Bojuka Bog): replay key pieces as soon as they hit your graveyard.

directions.win_conditions_note: Cuts Fraying Sanity and Agent Frank Horrigan for recursion; Muldrotha replays the remaining threats from the graveyard, but that is fewer finishers than stock. Add one back if you pick it.

recommendation: Counter Engine fits Mothman best: every mill trigger already gives counters, and these cards make each counter worth more. The removal package covers the deck's biggest weakness in every direction. All three directions stay under €20.

bracket3.name: Bracket 3 package
bracket3.rule: Bracket 3 (Upgraded) allows up to three Game Changers, no mass land denial, no chained extra turns, and game-ending two-card combos only late in the game.
bracket3.description: Mothman gets a trigger every time nonland cards are milled, by any player. This package makes mill happen constantly, turns milled creatures into damage, doubles your proliferate, adds a fourth way to win and gives the deck the counterspells it lacked.
notes: Mesmeric Orb mills you too, about one card for each of your permanents that untaps, and Struggle for Project Purity draws you about three more a turn. Play Orb when you can win within a few turns. If Gaea's Blessing is milled, it shuffles your graveyard, itself included, back into your library, so it only protects you while it is still in your library. Raul casts one spell a turn from what you milled that turn; The Master, Transcendent and Tato Farmer take milled creatures and lands from any graveyard.

Mesmeric Orb and The Water Crystal together make each opponent mill five cards for every permanent they untap, which empties a library in two or three turns. The Crystal only adds to opponents' mills, not yours. That is the top end of bracket 3. Tell your table, and leave one of the two out if it is too much.

Syr Konrad with Mindcrank or The Master of Lake-town can chain: damage makes opponents mill, and milled creature cards make Konrad deal damage again. With The Water Crystal each point of damage mills five, and Konrad's {1}{B} (each player mills a card) starts the chain on demand. It often ends the game. Bracket 3 allows a late-game combo like this (Konrad costs five), but tell your table.
Left out on purpose: Bloodchief Ascension. With Mindcrank it is a two-card infinite combo that can be ready on turn three or four. That is bracket 4 play.

swaps.why: Whenever a permanent untaps, its controller mills a card. Each one is a separate mill, so Mothman triggers many times a turn, on every player's turn, and The Water Crystal makes each opponent's mill five cards. It mills you too; Gaea's Blessing is the reset. In 62% of Mothman decks, and the most-played card this list was missing. Contagion Clasp needs four mana for each proliferate.

A second Mindcrank on a deathtouch body: any player who loses life, you included, mills that many cards, so rad life loss and combat damage feed Mothman, and it chains with Syr Konrad. Already owned (Bulk pile). Young Deathclaws is in 15% of Mothman decks.

Deals 1 damage to each opponent whenever another creature dies or a creature card is milled, by anyone. With the whole table milling that is steady damage, and with Mindcrank or The Master of Lake-town each hit mills more creature cards. In 51% of Mothman decks. Jason Bright (19%) needs your Mutants to die.

Every proliferate happens twice: rad counters on opponents and +1/+1 counters on your creatures both go up by two. A 3/5 flier for four. Harold and Bob is a 3/3 that turns into slow ramp when it dies.

Whenever an opponent would mill, they mill four more cards. Rad counters, Ruin Crab, Mindcrank and Mesmeric Orb all get the bonus, which makes running the table out of cards a real way to win. Tireless Tracker is in 10% of Mothman decks.
Two mana stops a board wipe or a combo, and bracket 3 tables play both; before this the deck had no counterspell. Hancock (32%) only pumps Zombies and Mutants, and only once it has counters.

Two mana at instant speed: counter a spell or destroy a creature whose mana value is no more than the number of cards in its controller's graveyard. In this deck graveyards fill within a few turns. Casualties of War costs six at sorcery speed.

Choose Sultai: draw a card the first time each turn a counter is put on one of your creatures. That includes opponents' turns, when Mothman triggers off their mills, so it is up to four cards a round for two mana. Harmonize is three cards once.

A fourth way to win. It gets a growth counter for every +1/+1 counter put on your creatures and wins the game at your upkeep with twenty. Hardened Scales, Branching Evolution and Corpsejack Menace speed it up, and proliferate adds to it. Contaminated Drink draws X cards but gives you rad counters.
A land that proliferates for four mana at instant speed. It replaces a land that enters tapped.

premium.why: Game Changer. Overloaded for seven mana it returns every nonland permanent your opponents control to their hands, at instant speed. Your creatures then attack into empty boards. Finality's wipe also shrinks your own creatures.

deck_changes.why: When Gaea's Blessing is milled it shuffles your graveyard, itself included, back into your library, so Mesmeric Orb milling you on every untap doesn't deck you. Radstorm was 4 mana and proliferates only once unless you cast other spells first that turn (storm), and with The Water Crystal opponents' rad counters are usually gone by your turn.

Destroys a nonland permanent an opponent controls, then fetches a Forest (a landfall for Ruin Crab and Evolution Sage), for one mana less. Already owned (loose pile). Vault 87's steal ends with the Saga.
